 Midterm Election Day in Evanston: Here’s what you need to know 
 One-stop shop of information and resources for Tuesday’s midterm election 
 by 
 Alex Harrison 
 November 2nd, 2026 November 2nd, 2026

Tuesday is Election Day across Illinois for the midterm general election, and polls will be open from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. If you are in line when polls close at 7 p.m., you are entitled to stay in line and still cast your vote. Here’s your one-stop shop for critical information and resources on how to vote, and what to expect when results roll in tonight.
 How can I vote in person Tuesday? 
 Evanston’s 45 precincts will be served by 26 polling sites on Election Day, and voters can find their polling site using the  county clerk’s online tool . Citywide voting is no longer available at the Robert Crown Community Center, 1801 Main St., because the early voting site has been converted to a local polling site for only two Evanston precincts.
 Illinois allows voters to register on Election Day at their local polling site. To do this, voters must provide two forms of documentation, one of which shows that they have lived at their current address for at least 30 days before Election Day. The  county clerk’s website  lists acceptable forms of identification.
 Full information on voting, registration and more can be found  in the Evanston RoundTable’s voting guide . (La versión en español  está disponible aquí .)
 I still have my mail ballot, what should I do? 
 The RoundTable strongly advises against depositing mail ballots in standard mailboxes on Election Day, as changes to postmark rules may result in those ballots not being counted, according to the county clerk’s office .
 Illinois requires that mail ballots be postmarked on or before Election Day to be valid and counted. The U.S. Postal Service changed its rules at the end of 2025 to consider mail collected from mailboxes as postmarked when it is processed at a regional Postal Service facility, which could be one or more days after it is dropped in a mailbox.
 To ensure your vote is counted, the RoundTable recommends using one of the following three options:
 Take your mail ballot to a post office and request a free manual postmark from the retail counter. Evanston has three post offices, located from north to south at 1929 Central St., 1101 Davis St. and 701 Main St. All three are open Tuesday from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.
 Deposit your mail ballot in a drop box at one of suburban Cook County’s six  Election Day Vote Centers ; the closest to Evanston is the Skokie Courthouse, 5600 Old Orchard Road. The mail ballot drop box at Robert Crown is no longer available, and Evanston voters cannot deposit their mail ballots at drop boxes in Chicago.
 Take your mail ballot to your local polling site and surrender it to an election judge. The judge will void the mail ballot and give you a regular ballot to vote with in person.
 What is on my ballot? 
 All Evanston voters will vote for federal and state legislators, including a new U.S. representative and U.S. senator and a new state senator in Springfield. Statewide executives, county officials, judges up for retention and numerous other races are also on the ballot. A full list of all candidates appearing on the ballot can be found  in the RoundTable’s ballot guide . (La versión en español  está disponible aquí .)
 How can I report issues I have while voting? 
 To inform our reporters of any issues you experience or observe while voting, email us at  tips@evanstonroundtable.com or leave us a voicemail at 847-864-7741.
 How can I share photos with the RoundTable? 
 Reader-submitted photos of voting or other Election Day activities can be emailed to  news@evanstonroundtable.com . Please do not take or send photos with your ballot selections visible; doing so is illegal in Illinois.
 When will results come in? 
 Initial results, including those from early votes and mail ballots that have already been counted, will not be reported publicly until after polls close at 7 p.m. The RoundTable will report on race calls from the Associated Press as they happen.
 Tuesday night’s results are unofficial and do not include numerous outstanding mail ballots, so tallies are expected to change over the next two weeks as these are counted. Mail ballots postmarked on or before Election Day can be received and counted through Nov. 17, and final results will be officially certified by the Illinois State Board of Elections on Nov. 24.
